pr_title: always execute condition for wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with
pr_body:
immediate=true

The API guarantees that the condition will be executed at least once independently of the context.



/kind bug
/kind regression
Fixes #118671


```release-note
wait.PollUntilContextTimeout function, if immediate is true, the condition will be invoked before waiting and guarantees that the condition is invoked at least once, regardless of whether the context has been cancelled.
```

/sig api-machinery

issue_context.title: wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true does not invoke condition function at least once
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Calling wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true does not invoke the passed condition function if context has already been cancelled.



### What did you expect to happen?

wait.PollUntilContextTimeout with immediate=true should invoke the passed condition function at least once even if context has already been cancelled as wait.PollUntilContextCancel documentation says:

> If immediate is true, condition will be invoked before waiting and guarantees that condition is invoked at least once, regardless of whether the context has been cancelled.

Note that wait.PollUntilContextTimeout wraps wait.PollUntilContextCancel, so the above should be applied to wait.PollUntilContextTimeout as well.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```go
package main

import (
        "context"
        "time"

        "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait"
)

func main() {
        err := wait.PollUntilContextTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second, 0, true, func(context.Context) (bool, error) {
                return true, nil
        })
        if err != nil {
                panic(err)
        }
}
```

This program panics because context ctx.Err is checked before invoking the passed function.


### Anything else we need to know?

The deprecated wait.PollImmediateWithContext does not have this kind of issue.
If wait.PollUntilContextTimeout is the replacement of wait.PollImmediateWithContext, it should exhibit the same behavior.
